newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Currency-led New Zealand debt markets end weaker.
newsitem.headline: Currency-led New Zealand debt markets end weaker.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (MAR) 92.52 (PREV 92.66) 90-DAYS 7.53 (PREV 7.43)
OVERNIGHT CASH 7.35 PCT (PREV 7.40) US 5-YR 6.15 (PREV 6.23)
* NZ debt markets end weak despite partial rebound in TWI * Short end worst-affected
* Bank bill futures actively traded
New Zealand short rates ended on their highs for the day after the market took fright from weakness in the New Zealand dollar and its Trade-Weighted Index, even though the TWI staged a late comeback.
The TWI was hit hard early in the session, losing 50 basis points at one stage, mostly on the back of wild swings in the U.S. dollar after the weekend's G-7 meeting.
By the close it had picked up some ground to end at 68.09 from Friday's close of 68.31.
"I guess they (bill rates) held in reasonably well, closing up about 10 points which is a weak close, but in terms of the performance of the TWI it's not bad," said one dealer.
The March bank bill futures contract dropped 14 basis points on the day to close at a crucial level of 92.52 on high turnover of 3,313 lots.
A close eye would be kept on the U.S. and New Zealand dollars overnight for direction, he said.
One other dealer said the day's trade represented a continuation of the recent trend.
"The curve continues to flatten while this currency/TWI takes a hammering. Local sentiment is still negative," he said.
Activity tapered off in the afternoon, apart from continued selling in the bill futures.
